One authenticated Copilot Studio agent on every SharePoint site

Standard-harness agent + Agents SDK web part on any number of sites, silent Entra SSO, user identity reaches the agent, sharing enforced (incl. revoke & re-grant).

The use case

What the customer built and observed

Goal: let authenticated employees chat with the same Copilot Studio agent from many SharePoint sites.

Customer setup (paraphrased)

  1. Agent deployed to Site A with the Copilot Studio SharePoint channel.
  2. On Site B, Site C and others: an Agent link web part pointing to that agent.
  3. Users are added (shared) on the agent.
  4. Users get access to Site A, Site B and every site where the agent appears.

Customer observations

  • Users can chat from any site that has the Agent link web part.
  • Removing a user from the agent blocks them (You don't have access to this agent); adding them back restores access.
  • Users must have access to Site A even when they use the agent from another site.
  • Same behaviour for users with and without a Microsoft 365 Copilot license.
Question: any concerns or potential issues with this approach?
Short answer: the approach is valid and supported (no code). We reproduced every observation. The real cost is the Site A dependency: it is a single point of failure and pushes you to over-grant Site A. Narrow it to Read on just the .agent file, or use the Agents SDK web part, which has no host-site dependency at all.
Two patterns, one runtime

How each pattern reaches the agent

Both end up in the same Copilot Studio runtime on api.powerplatform.com - the SharePoint channel's .agent file literally contains botSchema, environmentID and transport: "rest". That is why sharing, revocation and licensing behave the same; the difference is the extra hop through the file in Site A.

Answering the customer

Concerns and recommendations

high

Single point of failure in Site A

Every Agent link depends on the .agent file in the deployment site. Archiving/deleting Site A, changing its permissions, or a Site A member with Edit rights deleting or renaming the file breaks the agent on every site. Host it in a dedicated, locked-down "agent host" site or library.
high

Over-permissioning

"Users must have access to Site A" exposes Site A content to every agent user. Verified alternative: Read on only the .agent file (or a dedicated folder/library) - Site A stays Access Denied and the Agent link works.
medium

Two permission systems to keep in sync

Copilot Studio sharing and SharePoint file permissions. Drive both from one Entra security group.
medium

Misleading error message

Users who cannot read the .agent file see You need a Microsoft 365 Copilot license to access this agent - even though unlicensed users work. Brief the help desk.
medium

Capacity, not licenses

Copilot Studio agents in SharePoint "consume Copilot Studio capacity" - unlicensed users work, so plan and monitor capacity / pay-as-you-go.
low

One deployment site at a time

Copilot Studio: Only one SharePoint site can be deployed to at a time. Moving the host means undeploy/redeploy and re-pointing every Agent link.
low

Harness support

GitHub Copilot harness agents are not available for the SharePoint channel and not supported by the Agents SDK client today. Keep SharePoint-facing agents on the standard harness.
Recommended setup for the SharePoint-channel pattern: dedicated agent host site/library, one Entra security group used both for Copilot Studio sharing and for Read on the .agent file, minimal Edit rights, capacity monitoring. Choose the Agents SDK web part when you need no host-site dependency, inline/branded chat, several agents per page, programmatic control, or cannot grant access to the host site.
Build it

Step-by-step: the Microsoft 365 Agents SDK implementation

Exactly what was executed in the test tenant. Scripts and the SPFx solution are in the repository.

1

Build a standard-harness agent with Microsoft authentication

Copilot Studio home > Other ways to build > Agent (Standard). Add instructions. Settings > Security > Authentication = Authenticate with Microsoft (default). Optional: greet the user with {System.User.DisplayName} in the Conversation Start topic to prove identity flows through. Publish.
2

Copy the Microsoft 365 Agents SDK connection string

Standard UI: Channels > Web app (or Native app). New UI: right panel Channels (+) > App. The string identifies the environment and agent schema - no secret inside.
https://afdeda3552fae1459bc07b43e75630.0a.environment.api.powerplatform.com/copilotstudio/dataverse-backed/authenticated/bots/new_AgentAStandardharness/conversations?api-version=2022-03-01-preview
3

Share the agent with the people or security groups who may chat

Agent > Options (...) > Share > add users / groups with End user access. This list is enforced on every site (verified, including revoke and re-grant).
4

Register one Entra SPA app for the whole tenant (scripted)

Delegated Power Platform API / CopilotStudio.Copilots.Invoke + Graph basics, SPA redirect URI = the SharePoint origin (covers every site), tenant-wide consent. SPFx's built-in token provider cannot obtain this scope (sp-dev-docs #10775), so the web part uses MSAL.js with this app.
az login --tenant $TenantDomain --allow-no-subscriptions
.\scripts\New-AgentsSdkSpaApp.ps1 -TenantId $TenantDomain -SharePointRootUrl https://<tenant>.sharepoint.com
# -> appClientId 1f06ba87-...  adminConsent: granted
5

Build the SPFx package with tenant defaults (scripted)

SPFx 1.21.1 + @microsoft/agents-copilotstudio-client 1.9.1 + MSAL 4.30 + Bot Framework Web Chat 4.19.1, all bundled (no CDN, no API-access approvals). Node 22 required.
.\scripts\Build-SpfxPackage.ps1 -AppClientId <appClientId> -Version 1.0.1.0 -NodePath C:\tools\node-v22
# -> spfx-copilot-agent\sharepoint\solution\copilot-studio-agent-webpart.sppkg
6

Deploy once, tenant-wide

Add yourself as site admin of the app catalog (required even for SharePoint Administrators), upload the .sppkg, choose Enable this app and add it to all sites.
7

Add the web part to any page on any site

Edit page > + > Copilot Studio Agent (Agents SDK) > paste the connection string. App ID and tenant come from the package defaults. Repeat on as many sites as needed - or provision pages through the SharePoint pages REST API.
8

Grant normal SharePoint access

Visitor (Read) on the hosting site is enough. No access to any other site is required.
9

Validate

Greeting shows the user's name, the footer shows the signed-in UPN, unshared users get You don't have access to talk to this bot, and an anonymous call to the connection string returns HTTP 401.

Additional checks

  • Revocation: User B removed from Agent A -> blocked on next load; re-shared -> works again.
  • Anonymous POST to either connection string -> HTTP 401.
  • MFA users: silent SSO, no prompts; popup fallback never needed.
  • No tester had a Microsoft 365 Copilot or Copilot Studio license.

Reading the matrix

WORKS personalised greeting + on-topic answer. BLOCKED - not shared the agent replied You don't have access to talk to this bot. NOT SUPPORTED GitHub Copilot harness via Agents SDK. ANSWERS (no auth enforced) hosted embed answered regardless of sharing. ACCESS DENIED SharePoint page not accessible.

GitHub Copilot harness

What happened with the original Weather agent

Agents SDK: not supported (yet)

Every request - including from the agent owner - returned This action doesn't support agents built with the GitHub Copilot harness. Microsoft Learn: the Copilot Studio client library supports standard-harness agents only.

App-channel embed: renders but is not secured

The hosted web chat answered users the agent was not shared with and even a signed-out browser (anonymous Direct Line token). Treat the existing embed/button on the root site as public until this is enforced.
